touches.text: A device talks to other devices only over the bus, never by importing them.
The exceptions are client tools a device publishes:

Trouble: it has to be able to report when nothing else can, so a direct line makes sense for recovery (6.3.4). [Q#86: Proofs in tester, codemother and librarian (8 imports, measured 2026-11-11) stand up a scratch bus in their own process by importing the cairn device's bus machine (BusDevice.scratch, BusShim), so they can drive their shim against stub devices. Does the cairn device get a fourth exception here, a published scratch-bus tool for proofs? Or do those teeth ride the live bus through bus_client and lose their stubs? CC's read: publish it. A proof needs a bus it controls, and db_domain's published client already carries scratch() the same way.]

Its web panel is the operator's to-do list: email, trouble tickets, open questions (the ones only the operator can answer). The list is live: items appear as they arrive and leave as they're answered or resolved.
Machine: the operator inbox builds the to-do list from live state, storing nothing (the operator_inbox tool, 17.14).
import_sieve: one parse of every .py into an import graph; what reaches what. WHY: enforces "only the proxy reaches the host/database" and RULE 1 by physics. USERS: CodeMother, the inference proxy.

The RULE 1 check is a path check: code inside device bar may not import cairn.devices.foo (anything not under cairn.devices.bar), except a tool foo publishes (cairn.devices.foo.tools.<x>, its charter saying published_by_device). Inside one device there is one owner, so nothing is checked there. A charter's public_interface describes what the component offers (modules, functions, bus verbs, commands); the check does not read it. Akien 2026-11-09 (Q#77): "wouldn't it be easier (for the python code anyway) to see if the imports do not include other device paths?"
operator_inbox: builds the operator's to-do list from live state, storing nothing (7.3.7). USERS: Operator.
